note: Real package the model produced for /interactive-visualizer-in-chat of coulomb force and charge on 2026-08-30. The runtime worker browser-tested it as ready with a schemaVersion 2 manifest; the Next gate rejected it because validManifest only accepted schemaVersion 1.

plan.title: Coulomb Force Lab
plan.objective: Let learners manipulate two point charges and their separation to see how Coulomb's law sets force magnitude and whether the charges attract or repel.
plan.rationale: A flat two-charge diagram makes sign, distance, equal-and-opposite force vectors, and the inverse-square relationship readable at once.
assumptions: The charges behave as point charges in vacuum.
Only the electrostatic interaction between two charges is modeled.
Visual spacing is scaled so the charge symbols remain legible.

controls.label: Charge q1
controls.purpose: Set the magnitude and sign of the first charge.

controls.label: Charge q2
controls.purpose: Set the magnitude and sign of the second charge.

controls.label: Separation r
controls.purpose: Set the center-to-center separation between the charges.

controls.label: Play or pause
controls.purpose: Animate markers along the force-vector directions.

controls.label: Reset
controls.purpose: Restore the initial charges and separation.

outputs.label: Force magnitude
outputs.purpose: Show the force calculated from Coulomb's law.

outputs.label: Interaction
outputs.purpose: Identify attraction, repulsion, or zero force.

outputs.label: Separation
outputs.purpose: Show the current distance between charge centers.

interactions: Move either charge slider through negative, zero, and positive values.
Change separation with the range control or drag either charge symbol horizontally.
Use arrow keys while the canvas is focused to adjust separation.
Play or pause directional markers without changing the calculation.
Reset all values to the initial example.
dataRequirements: Convert microcoulombs to coulombs before calculating force.
accessibilityRequirements: Provide native labels and live numeric outputs for every range control.
Expose a dynamic text alternative for the canvas.
Support keyboard control of separation and visible focus indicators.
Start paused when reduced motion is requested.
Keep all controls and labels usable at 375 CSS pixels.

manifest.title: Coulomb Force Lab
manifest.description: An interactive two-charge model showing Coulomb-force magnitude, attraction or repulsion, and inverse-square distance dependence.
manifest.accessibilityDescription: A labelled two-dimensional diagram of two charges with equal and opposite force arrows. Sliders control each charge and their separation; the canvas also supports drag and keyboard distance adjustment. Live outputs report force, interaction type, and distance.

assumptions: Charges are treated as point charges in vacuum.
Only the electrostatic interaction between the two displayed charges is included.
Diagram spacing is scaled for legibility; the numeric separation drives the calculation.
limitations: The moving markers indicate force direction but do not integrate particle motion.
Medium, relativistic, and quantum effects are omitted.
Force-arrow length is compressed for readability; use the numeric output for magnitude.

semanticTests.name: visual integrity
semanticTests.assertion: At desktop and 375 CSS pixel widths, the interface has no horizontal overflow or clipped text; labels and controls do not overlap; token-derived foregrounds remain legible on host surfaces; both force arrows start at the exact named charge-edge anchors; and the separation line ticks share the exact charge-center x-coordinates.

semanticTests.name: Coulomb calculation
semanticTests.assertion: The displayed magnitude equals 8.9875517923e9 × abs(q1 × q2) × 1e-12 / r² and updates after every slider, drag, keyboard, or reset action.

semanticTests.name: force direction
semanticTests.assertion: Like nonzero signs point both force arrows away from the other charge, unlike signs point both arrows toward the other charge, and either zero charge removes both arrows and reports zero force.

semanticTests.name: equal and opposite vectors
semanticTests.assertion: The two force arrows always use the same rendered length and opposite directions for every nonzero state.

semanticTests.name: interaction accessibility
semanticTests.assertion: All three ranges have native labels and linked outputs, the canvas has a current descriptive aria-label and keyboard distance controls, and focus indicators remain visible.

semanticTests.name: animation controls
semanticTests.assertion: The play-pause button exposes exactly one state icon at a time and synchronizes aria-label and aria-pressed; reset restores q1 = 4 µC, q2 = -6 µC, and r = 0.8 m.

semanticTests.name: motion and theme behavior
semanticTests.assertion: Reduced-motion users start paused, animation work stops while the document is hidden, and a breadboard:themechange event rereads host tokens and repaints the canvas.
